description.summary: Hybrid Retrieval combines complementary retrieval signals so a RAG system can search with more than one matching strategy.
description.description: Hybrid Retrieval is a RAG technique that retrieves candidates from more than one retrieval approach, commonly keyword matching and dense vector similarity, and then combines the candidate results before context assembly.
description.problemStatement: A single retrieval method can miss useful context when a query depends on exact terminology, semantic similarity, or both.
description.coreIdea: Run complementary retrievers and merge their ranked candidates so later RAG stages can work from a broader candidate pool.

inputRequirements.name: Retrievable corpus
inputRequirements.description: A corpus available through at least two retrieval signals or retriever configurations.

outputArtifacts.name: Merged retrieval candidates
outputArtifacts.description: A candidate set produced by combining results from complementary retrieval methods.

implementationConsiderations: Use a deterministic merge or fusion strategy so retrieval experiments can be compared consistently.
evaluationGuidance: Compare retrieval recall and candidate quality against each individual retrieval method.
